headline: Committee advances school wastewater deal and zoning cleanup

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The committee recommended a temporary wastewater deal for a new Central Maui school and a zoning change for six parcels.
meeting.recap: The committee took up Bill 116, an agreement for temporary wastewater service to a new Central Maui school.[[0:06:02]] The school is expected to open in 2031.[[0:06:15]] If the county's new wastewater plant is not running by then, the existing Wailuku-Kahului plant would take up to 14,500 gallons a day.[[0:06:28]] A testifier urged against adding flow to the existing plant until it has effective disinfection.[[0:15:53]] The environmental management director said the new plant should be running before the school needs service in July 2031.[[0:18:44]] Members voted 9–0 to recommend passing the bill on first reading.[[0:28:13]] Resolution 26-137 would send a zoning change for six parcels to the Maui Planning Commission for review.[[0:28:35]] A consultant for the landowners said the change would make the whole property B2 business zoning.[[0:37:34]] He said the owners are not proposing any new development.[[0:39:22]] Members voted 8–0 to recommend adopting the resolution, with one member excused.[[1:04:39]] The program began in July 2024.[[1:10:36]] Three volunteer groups now take part.[[1:12:25]] The committee deferred the item, setting it aside for now, with no objections.[[1:26:50]]

issues.oneLine: Bill 116 would set up temporary wastewater service for a new Central Maui school.
issues.why: The director called the agreement a Plan B in case the county's new wastewater plant is not running when the school opens.

deadlines.t: New Central Maui school needs wastewater service.

issues.next: The bill moves to the full Council.
issues.brief: The new Central Maui wastewater plant is projected to begin operating in late 2029 or later.[[#1]] The temporary service at the existing plant would be up to 14,500 gallons a day, subject to available capacity.[[#2]] The director said the county has environmental permits for the new plant and is working through land approvals.[[#3]] A testifier said the Kahului plant stopped all disinfection in 2018.[[#4]]
